description: We are Team Quantum Builders  from Bangladesh. We built a bilingual (English/বাংলা) climate app that turns 45 years of NASA Earth data into trends people can trust, plus live flood, heat and disaster alerts. Our skills: full-stack web development (Next.js, TypeScript), climate data analysis and statistics, satellite maps and video. We care about climate risk in Bangladesh. We welcome teammates in data science, remote sensing, UI/UX design or science communication.
summary: EarthScope is a bilingual (English and বাংলা) climate web app that turns 45 years of NASA Earth observations into trends anyone can check, built for Bangladesh, where heat, floods and sea-level rise hit hardest. It helps students, citizens and local planners see what is changing where they live, how fast, and whether the change is real. It tests every trend statistically, removes artificial jumps in the data, and cross-checks NASA POWER against ECMWF ERA5 and rain-gauge records. Alongside the trends it tracks live disasters, river floods, heat and air quality, finds the nearest shelters, and produces a printable climate report.
details: Most climate apps take satellite data at face value. EarthScope is an Earth-system trend detective built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge that rigorously tests what is changing, where, and by how much—while weeding out sensor artefacts that mislead naive models. Using 45 years of NASA observations, it uncovers counterintuitive planetary mechanisms, like how dry-season irrigation in Bangladesh cools farmland by day while warming it at night, and provides live multi-hazard tracking and shelter routing in both English and Bangla.
